title: Chinese AI models surge in global popularity
content:
AI was a major focus as U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met this week.
The most advanced U.S. models lead most benchmarks, but Chinese companies like DeepSeek, Z.ai and Alibaba have released new models with major performance gains in tasks such as coding.
According to usage data shared with CNBC, the global adoption of Chinese models by companies has increased substantially in 2026.
Chinese AI models have gone from a relatively small share of usage to a majority on two major developer platforms that provide gateways for companies to access models from different providers. On OpenRouter, they accounted for 57%-67% of tokens used in the week of Sept. 14, up from 6%-13% in February. On Vercel, their share rose to 55% in August from 11% in January.
OpenRouter's data related to companies in the U.S., Europe and what it defines as the "Global South" — 82 countries across Central and South America, Africa, and Asia. Vercel did not specify its data's geographical breakdown.
Concern is growing in Washington, where two U.S. House Committees are investigating the impact of rising adoption of Chinese models.
The U.S. has sought to preserve its AI lead by restricting Chinese AI companies from buying the most advanced chips through export controls.
Washington is concerned about them accessing Nvidia chips remotely, via overseas data centers, and gaining ground by using "distillation" where new models mimic older, more established ones.
Chinese AI represents "real economic and security risks for the United States," said Daniel Remler, a senior fellow in the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security (CNAS), a think tank.
"The ultimate concern is that the integration of Chinese AI models pulls countries into a Chinese technology sphere of influence that hardens into geopolitical alignment," he told CNBC.
Peter Walker, head of insights at OpenRouter, told CNBC, Chinese open source models released this year "can credibly perform in advanced agentic use cases, especially in regards to coding, in a way that was just not true in late 2025."
They're also "incredibly cost-effective compared to most models from American labs," he added.
Earlier this week, OpenAI and Anthropic both announced new, cheaper models. Dianne Penn, head of product management, research and labs at Anthropic, told CNBC that the company was trying to make its models answers "more efficient, so it uses less tokens depending on your effort setting."
Price is key in rising adoption of Chinese models, Harpreet Arora, head of agentic infrastructure at Vercel, told CNBC. "Chinese models are becoming capable enough for more tasks at a much lower cost. Once a model meets the quality bar for the job, that price difference becomes compelling."
But he added that companies still want to use frontier U.S. models for some more complicated tasks.
Businesses in what OpenRouter defines as "Global South" have been the biggest users of Chinese AI models on the company's system in recent weeks.
More than two-thirds — 67% — of the tokens these companies use are on Chinese models. About half the tokens on OpenRouter are used by companies in the U.S.
"Southeast Asia in particular may see significant uptake of Chinese AI models given the close economic and cultural linkages [with China] plus growing digital infrastructure," said CNAS' Remler.
"Anywhere from Lagos to São Paulo to Jakarta where entrepreneurs and governments are looking for cheap, open models, will look first to Chinese AI."

report.summary: Chinese AI models now account for a majority of business token usage on developer gateways OpenRouter and Vercel, driven by low prices and strong coding performance.
report.background: Through 2025 and 2026, Washington tried to slow China's AI progress with export controls on advanced chips, while U.S. labs like OpenAI and Anthropic kept the strongest benchmark scores. Chinese firms — DeepSeek, Z.ai, Alibaba's Qwen and others — took a different route: releasing capable open-weight models, optimizing for cost, and iterating fast on coding and agentic tasks. That combination started winning over businesses that only need a model to clear a quality bar at a fraction of frontier pricing. Adoption data from OpenRouter and Vercel now shows the shift clearly, and it landed just as Presidents Trump and Xi met with AI high on the agenda. U.S. lawmakers are investigating whether cheap Chinese models create dependency, data exposure, and geopolitical alignment risks.
key_points: Usage flipped fast: on OpenRouter, Chinese models went from 6%-13% of tokens in February to 57%-67% in the week of Sept. 14. On Vercel, their share rose from 11% in January to 55% in August — moving from niche to majority on two major multi-model gateways.

Capability caught up with price: OpenRouter's Peter Walker says 2026-era Chinese open source models now perform credibly in advanced agentic and coding workloads, something he says simply wasn't true in late 2025. Combined with much lower cost, that makes them the default pick for many teams.

Emerging markets lead adoption: On OpenRouter, companies in the 'Global South' — 82 countries across Latin America, Africa and Asia — route 67% of their tokens to Chinese models. Analysts expect Southeast Asia to be a particularly strong growth area due to economic, cultural and infrastructure links.

Washington is alarmed: two U.S. House committees are investigating the adoption trend. Think-tank analysts warn the real risk is that model integration pulls countries into a Chinese tech sphere that hardens into geopolitical alignment.

U.S. labs are responding on price: OpenAI and Anthropic both shipped cheaper models this week, with Anthropic emphasizing token efficiency. Vercel's Harpreet Arora says price becomes decisive once a model meets the quality bar for a job.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this marks the end of the assumption that frontier quality alone wins the market. A large, price-sensitive middle tier of workloads — coding assistants, agents, internal automation — is migrating to open-weight Chinese models, pressuring U.S. labs' margins and pushing them toward cheaper, more token-efficient tiers. For developers, it means real multi-model flexibility: the same gateway can route routine tasks to a $0.20-per-million-token model and reserve frontier U.S. models for hard reasoning. For regular users, the practical effect is cheaper AI products and more capable free tiers, especially outside the U.S. and Europe. The strategic risk is dependency: if toolchains, fine-tunes and data pipelines standardize on Chinese weights, switching costs — and policy exposure — rise sharply.
report.tools: To follow this trend, watch OpenRouter and Vercel AI Gateway, which publish cross-model usage data and let you A/B test providers in one API. On the model side, evaluate DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen, Z.ai's GLM and Moonshot's Kimi for coding and agentic work. For self-hosting, use Hugging Face for weights, plus Ollama for local prototyping and vLLM or SGLang for production serving. Pair them with agent frameworks like LangGraph or the OpenAI-compatible SDKs most Chinese models now support.
